solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One third of fruit's been eaten? Get stuck in

indicators.note: what has been eaten is no longer there, so that third of the fruit disappears

parts.note: a greengage is a green plum
the first three of its nine letters, the part eaten

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bitten piece of fruit and urges a companion to tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'been eaten' is the instruction, not part of a picnic: a third of the plum is bitten off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to get stuck in, British slang for throwing yourself into a task or fight, is to join battle.

clue.text: I think I'm in the wrong dance

definitions.text: I think I'm in the wrong
definitions.meaning: the polite phrase that opens a correction or apology
an old ballroom dance where anyone may tap a shoulder and cut in

explanation.surface: A flustered dancer realises they have wandered into the wrong dance.
explanation.walkthrough: An excuse-me is an old-fashioned ballroom dance in which you may tap a dancer's shoulder and claim their partner; the phrase is also how you politely admit a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the phrase said when owning up to a blunder, and the ballroom dance named after the words used to cut in.

clue.text: Roman emperor good with Scotland

parts.note: Alba is the Gaelic name for Scotland

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor teams up with Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: he ruled briefly after Nero, in the year of four emperors, AD 69.

clue.text: Partly engineering a machine to remove cotton seeds

definitions.text: a machine to remove cotton seeds

indicators.note: only part of the next word is used, so look inside it

parts.note: letters three to five of this word

explanation.surface: A description of a cotton gin as a piece of engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the only word that looks like part of the definition, which is why the hiding place is easy to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary definition: Eli Whitney's 1793 cotton engine, shortened to gin, pulls fibre away from seed.

clue.text: Second key Oscar and BAFTA, say, for original direction of Titanic

parts.note: both are film prizes; 'say' marks them as examples

explanation.surface: Film-prize talk about the movie Titanic, which won eleven Oscars.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about the film; the definition is about the ship. 'Oscar' is not O here: the whole phrase is one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: the liner set out from Southampton heading toward open ocean, and never made port.

clue.text: Queen one earl upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, its letters tumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: A queen has upset one of her earls.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleanor of Aquitaine and Eleanor of Castile were both English queens.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a royal name borne by several medieval English consorts.

clue.text: Crop weight reduced during unseasonable warmth

indicators.note: a word reduced is cut down to its standard abbreviation
one thing happening during another sits within it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: warmth at the cold time of year is out of season
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A farmer worries that a warm spell out of season has cut the weight of the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The farming surface makes 'reduced' look like a smaller yield; it only shortens a word to one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cereal sown in autumn to overwinter and be harvested the next summer.

clue.text: Be frightened under cars being repaired

indicators.note: something being repaired is taken apart and put back together, here in a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic is nervous about lying under cars while they are being fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The garage picture makes 'under' look like a position, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to behave in a panicky way, as if fleeing from a threat.

clue.text: Saw Twitter introducing a letter signifying unknown

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring in, so the second part goes into the first

parts.note: A, plus Y, a letter used in algebra for an unknown

explanation.surface: A social-media post that brings in the letter used for an unknown, as in X or Y.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitter' with its capital T looks like the social network, but here it is birdsong. 'Saw' is the noun, not the past of see.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned sense: a saw is a proverb, a wise old maxim.

clue.text: Director and unsubtle actor get ready in the UAE

parts.note: DIRECTOR cut short to its first three letters
a ham is an actor who overplays

explanation.surface: A film director and an over-the-top actor prepare to shoot in the Emirates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not prepared but a noun: ready money, cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword sense of ready, meaning cash, pinned to a place: the currency of the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: A sign of spring — family eat outside house at last

indicators.note: the family and the eating stay outside, wrapping around the next piece
at last means at the very end, so take only the final letter

parts.note: a clan is a family group

explanation.surface: An early-spring family meal eaten outdoors, outside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two pieces run together and wrap round the single letter, which lands just after the opening C.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lesser celandine is a little yellow flower among the first to bloom each year.

clue.text: Be very protective of girl in US city

indicators.note: the girl is in the city, so her letters sit inside its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A parent is anxious about a daughter living in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb, to fuss over someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb from the noun: to treat someone as a children's nurse would, coddling them.

clue.text: Bread or dough? No big difference

definitions.meaning: bread and dough are both slang for money, here the loose coins kind

explanation.surface: A baker shrugs that bread and dough are much the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The baking picture hides that bread and dough are both slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: coins in the pocket, money in slang; and, read word by word, an alteration that is only slight.

clue.text: Queen not wanting to be spotted on stage?

definitions.text: Queen not wanting to be spotted on stage?

parts.note: a royal who wishes to avoid something
surface: seen in the theatre; meant: a queen in a play whose hand is marked with a spot of blood she cannot wash off

explanation.surface: A royal who hopes no one will notice her on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' seems to mean seen; it means marked with a spot, the bloodstain she tries to scrub from her hands in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue: Shakespeare's Scottish queen is desperate to be rid of the spot of blood on her hand.

clue.text: Have the ability to finish off academic article

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its end, so take the letter it finishes with

explanation.surface: A scholar able to complete a paper for a journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like the paper being finished, but it is the grammatical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the modal verb of being able.

clue.text: A check on waterproof road surface

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'A check on waterproof' puts the check after, on the end of, the raincoat

parts.note: a dam checks a river's flow

explanation.surface: An inspection to confirm a road's surface keeps water out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterproof' reads as an adjective for the road; it is the noun, a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary sense: the compacted broken-stone paving named after John McAdam.

clue.text: Country long showing significant growth

parts.note: to pine for is to long for

explanation.surface: A country showing strong economic growth over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' sounds economic; it is a plant. 'Long' is a verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: the monkey puzzle tree, a large conifer, is literally something grown, and a big one.

clue.text: Deserts, concerned with local political division

definitions.note: Deserts is plural as in 'just deserts'; REWARD is singular

parts.note: a ward is an electoral district of a town

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a cause out of worry over local ward politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' looks like a verb, abandons; it is the noun in 'just deserts', stressed like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: your deserts are what you have earned, good or bad, so the positive side fits.

clue.text: Twerk for dancing? This must be cut out

indicators.note: dancing letters jig about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of twerking and wants it banned from the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' sounds like stop it; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: ornamental patterns sawn out of thin wood with a fine saw are, by nature, cut out.

clue.text: Column briefly mentions iconic characters primarily associated with the cinema

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: FILE (a column of people) without its last letter

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letters

parts.note: first letters of Mentions Iconic Characters

explanation.surface: A newspaper column name-drops iconic film characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' is not newspaper writing but a file, a line of people one behind another.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adjective for things of or like the movies.

clue.text: Preserved vessel lost power

explanation.surface: A historic ship kept as a museum piece that has lost its engine power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserved' calls up a museum ship; it is fruit kept in sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrower sense: fruit or peel kept by steeping in sugar syrup.

clue.text: Character Ibsen created in Councillor, a big cheese?

indicators.note: the character is created in the councillor, so her name goes inside

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for councillor
Hedda Gabler, heroine of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: A theatre figure asks whether a local councillor is really an important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big cheese' means a bigwig, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example, with a wink: the Somerset hard cheese is traditionally made in large wheels.

clue.text: Compel using spoken Gaelic when having company over

indicators.note: in a down entry, something over sits above, so the company comes first
a spoken word is heard, not seen, so take its sound and spell it another way

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Gaelic

explanation.surface: Forcing guests to speak Gaelic when they come round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having company over' paints a dinner party; it just places one piece on top of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to force someone to act by pressure or threat.

clue.text: Friend had sense of taste

explanation.surface: A friend with good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' seems to be possession; it is eating, as in 'had lunch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A transferred sense: the roof of the mouth, once thought the seat of taste, came to mean the faculty itself.

clue.text: One step saving leader

indicators.note: 'saving' can mean except, as in 'saving your presence', so the leader is left out

explanation.surface: A single step that rescues a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' reads as rescuing but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the card or die face with a single pip counts as one.

clue.text: State current saving after what HS2 no longer will do to Leeds?

parts.words: what HS2 no longer will do to Leeds
parts.note: the HS2 high-speed rail line's eastern leg to Leeds was scrapped
I is the symbol for electric current
a saving is a cut in spending

explanation.surface: A complaint about the British government's cost-cutting on the HS2 rail line.
explanation.walkthrough: HS2 is a British high-speed railway whose Leeds leg was cancelled to save money. The clue lists pieces out of order: 'after' puts the railway phrase first.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the six New England states of the US.

clue.text: Terrier — mine's escaped from Pacific island

indicators.note: what has escaped from somewhere is no longer in it, so the mine leaves the island

parts.note: home of the Bounty mutineers' descendants
a pit is a mine, removed

explanation.surface: A dog that has run away from a mine on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine's' reads as possessive, my dog; it is 'mine has', a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small, shaggy Scottish breed of terrier.

clue.text: Almost every diver wanting protection for breathing

indicators.note: almost all of a word is the word just short of complete, so drop its last letter
a word lacking protection has lost its outer letters, the shell around its middle

parts.note: DIVER without its outer letters D and R

explanation.surface: Nearly every diver lacks breathing apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protection' looks like diving gear; it is the outside of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything still drawing breath is living.

clue.text: Unknown coin got in change

indicators.note: as a verb, to change the letters is to swap them round

explanation.surface: A strange coin turned up among someone's loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like coins, matching 'coin', but it tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: travelling under a false identity, so not recognised.

clue.text: Idol in precious metal, not large

explanation.surface: A statue of a false god cast in precious metal, but not a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: The golden calf is the idol the surface calls up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an object of worship, a deity or its image.

clue.text: What cuts light from space views? Pluto mainly

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so all but the last letter

parts.note: to eye is to view, so eyes = views
Hades, the Greek counterpart of Pluto, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Astronomy talk: what blocks the light from space in pictures of Pluto?
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto is the god of the underworld, not the dwarf planet; the Greeks called him Hades. 'Space' is only the room in front of your face.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a visor worn on the brow that blocks glare from the open air around you.

clue.text: Shifting sand blocks Greek port

indicators.note: shifting sand moves about, its letters landing in a new order
the sand blocks the abbreviation by sitting in its middle

explanation.surface: Drifting sand is silting up a harbour in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek setting is a decoy: the port is Polish, on the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a major Baltic seaport in northern Poland.
